 Gold rate in Kolkata on November 4: check 22, 18 and 24 karat rates before Dhanteras and Diwali shopping
 By Upstox News Desk 2 min read | Updated on November 04, 2026, 17:18 IST
 Preferred news source Select Upstox as your Preferred news source SUMMARY
 Kolkata gold rates were ₹13,965 a gram for 24 karat, ₹12,801 for 22 karat and ₹10,474 for 18 karat on Wednesday, amid showrooms reporting heavier enquiries this week
 Gold prices have risen slightly on Wednesday, compared to Tuesday. | Image: Shutterstock
 Gold rates in Kolkata were ₹13,965 per gram for 24 karat, ₹12,801 for 22 karat and ₹10,474 for 18 karat on Wednesday, November 4 at the time of writing. 
 Open FREE Demat Account within minutes! Join now 
 Ten grams works out to ₹1,39,650, ₹1,28,010 and ₹1,04,738 for 24k, 22k and 18k gold respectively.
 Purity Rate per gram Rate per 10 g Change from Nov 3 (per 10 gram) 
 24K (999) ₹13,965 ₹1,39,650 +₹270 (+0.19%) 
 22K (916) ₹12,801 ₹1,28,010 +₹250 (+0.20%) 
 18K (750) ₹10,474 ₹1,04,738 +₹200 (+0.19%) 
 Gold rates in Kolkata on November 4, 2026; indicative, before making charges and GST 
 Dhanteras falls on Friday, November 6, and Diwali on Sunday, November 8, and Bowbazar's bullion lane, showrooms along Camac Street and other markets are already reporting heavier enquiries.
 Wednesday's session added ₹270 per 10 grams to 24 karat and ₹250 to 22 karat, recovering a small part of the 3.51% slide on October 31. Gold is still about ₹12,000 per 10 grams below October's peak of ₹1,51,570, which dealers say has brought back buyers who held off during the rally.
 Kolkata's preference runs to lightweight, design-heavy jewellery, so 18 and 22 karat do most of the volume, with 24 karat reserved for coins and gifting.
 Bengali bridal sets in 22 karat remain the biggest single purchase category. Buyers here increasingly ask for the making charge as a rupee figure per gram rather than a percentage, a habit that makes cross-shop comparison far easier.
 The rates are indicative and a particular store may quote differently. So buyers should compare rates at more than one jeweller on their own. The final bill will also be higher than the karat-based price because making charges and 3% GST are added.
 Before buying, one should compare making charges store to store, ask about exchange terms if you plan to trade in old gold, and confirm a BIS hallmark with a six-digit HUID on every piece.
